why: I checked the PASS and FAIL conditions of both verifier checks against their expect lines. Check 1 passes only if the call on invalid JSON "does not throw" and prints `{}`. It fails if an error escapes, the result isn't an empty object, loadConfig isn't in src/config.js, or "the parse error is not caught inside loadConfig". Each of these follows from "catches the JSON.parse error and returns {} instead". The step that confirms the function is exported only makes the import-based run possible; it adds no stricter rule. Check 2 passes if every test passes, and fails if a test fails or npm test exits non-zero or can't run. All of that follows from "npm test passes". The stricter checks all sit under "Advisory (does not decide PASS or FAIL)": valid JSON still loading, a missing file still throwing, the old test being replaced, the stderr warning, the README update and the app.js run. No condition requires exact wording or file scope.
